- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1), model underestimates upward momentum → add 2–4% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile → adjust downward by 1–3% for short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to lag → delay peak forecast by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean reversion → reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or flat.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often fails to capture momentum → increase forecast slope by 1–2% per day.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early horizon → apply sentiment smoothing (avg of last 3 sentiment values) to adjust forecast bias.
